newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica off lows, may gain on U.S. deal.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica off lows, may gain on U.S. deal.

text.p: Shares in Telefonica de Espana were lower but still outperforming the Ibex-35 blue chip index on Monday, as the market awaited clarification of an expected tie-up with U.S. operator MCI, dealers said.
A Portugal Telecom statement earlier today referred to a joint venture between the Spanish and U.S. firms to be announced today.
An MCI official said later this reference was "an error," but declined to comment on whether a deal had been reached, as widely expected by analysts.
At 0945 GMT, Telefonica was down 10 pesetas, 0.29 percent, to 3,405 while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares fell 0.68 percent to 5,404.39.
A possible deal between Telefonica and MCI has been partly discounted, but the stock may yet see further upside on confirmation, dealers said.
The stock is still likely to outperform the share indices, although much will depend on Wall Street, one said.
"If the market was neutral I'd say Telefonica could add 50-100 pesetas short-term. But in any case I'd still buy against the Ibex," said Fadi Ismail, a trader at Credit Lyonnais Securities.
However volatility on Wall Street, which has been hit by fears of rising interest rates, will likely continue to spill over to Madrid.
"I can't see it testing next resistance within the next couple of weeks, saving big surprises," Ismail added.
Nearest support was pegged at 3,360 pesetas, with next resistance at 3,465 pesetas.
A dealer at a foreign brokerage said although the news of an American alliance would be positive for the shares, they should not necessarily outperform.

"I don't think a deal has been discounted totally, simply because no-one's really been able to analyse what this might actually mean for the shares. But I shouldn't think there are reasons for it to do better than the market," he said.
He added that few final international clients had been very active in Spain recently, and it might take some time for them to come back into the market given volatility.
